clue.text: Study by country's leading economist

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
the US is a country

indicators.note: leading points to the front letter of the word economist

explanation.surface: A national economic study carried out by the country's top economist.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s of country's is just a link; 'by' is the Latin PER.
explanation.definitionFit: To read through carefully is to study, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Frank's a tool they say

indicators.note: they say means as people pronounce it, a sound-alike signal

parts.note: a plane is a woodworking tool

explanation.surface: A man called Frank being described as a tool, rude slang for an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain speaking is candid and direct, so plain and frank are synonyms.

clue.text: Try wearing torn clothing

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the ripped word goes round the attempt word

parts.note: rent means torn, as in a garment rent apart
aim means try, as in aim to do

explanation.surface: Putting on ripped clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic or literary word for clothing and garments.

clue.text: Continue doggedly with idols Nero replaced

indicators.note: replaced means put back in different places, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Emperor Nero carrying on stubbornly as his idols are swapped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Persisting through difficulty is the phrasal verb's meaning, a synonym for keeping going.

clue.text: Cheap containers

definitions.meaning: a tin and a pot are both containers

explanation.surface: Bargain-bin receptacles on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot describes something shoddy or of little worth, hence cheap; read as two words it is a pair of vessels.

clue.text: Furious with deserter found in the middle of Amiens

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so the deserter goes inside
the middle of picks the central two letters of Amiens

parts.note: a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Anger at a deserter discovered in the centre of the French city of Amiens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is the container signal; Amiens is a French city whose name supplies only its central pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Very angry, enraged: a straight synonym.

clue.text: Saw priest in preference to bishop

parts.note: over means in preference to, as in chosen over
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: Choosing a priest rather than a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same sense as a pithy adage.

clue.text: Material of value mostly returned to poet

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the shortened value word is read backwards
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: rate means value, as in rate highly
Tom Paulin is a Northern Irish poet

explanation.surface: Something of value handed back to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the value word before 'returned' turns it round; the poet is Tom Paulin, a name solvers outside Britain and Ireland may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof fabric, so a kind of material.

clue.text: Insect endlessly eating into house plant

indicators.note: one thing eating into another sits within it, so the shortened insect goes inside the house

parts.note: a villa is a house

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the insect word

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug chewing its way into a house plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House plant' reads as one thing, but 'house' belongs to the wordplay and only 'plant' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is a climbing orchid, so it is a plant as well as the flavouring from its pods.

clue.text: Works as party secretary at first

parts.note: Labour is a British political party

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word secretary

explanation.surface: Someone serving as a party's secretary, describing their job.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of the UK's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: To labour is to work hard, so labours and works are matching verbs.

clue.text: Fool about after lips met excitedly

indicators.note: after means the about word comes behind the rearranged letters
excitedly suggests agitation, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone fooling about after a passionate kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool about' reads as a phrasal verb, but it splits: 'Fool' defines and 'about' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, gullible person, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Unsettled by endless touring Sheeran retired

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the endless word wraps the other piece

parts.note: infinite means endless

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ed Sheeran is the English singer-songwriter

explanation.surface: A singer who has given up endless touring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' looks like it describes the touring, but it supplies the outer word; 'retired' means the singer's name goes backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not fixed or decided is unsettled, a synonym.

clue.text: One having an edge over Miles in test

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the edged tool is read backwards

parts.note: an axe is a tool with a cutting edge

explanation.surface: Someone holding an advantage over a rival named Miles in a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having an edge' looks like 'holding an advantage', but it describes a bladed tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A test of knowledge or skill is an examination, of which this is the short form.

clue.text: Safe-breaking expert not unknown

indicators.note: breaking means smashing up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not means the unknown letter is left out

parts.note: X is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A specialist safecracker who is not some stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' removes X from EXPERT, leaving EPERT for 'breaking' to rearrange. 'Safe-breaking' reads as one word, but the hyphen hides a split: 'Safe' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter is old criminal slang for a safe or strongbox.

clue.text: Advocate removing power from adversary in support of prince

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece in support of another holds it up from beneath, so it comes after
removing means the power letter is taken out

parts.note: an opponent is an adversary
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: An advocate who removes power from a rival while backing a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the adversary's two P's is taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues in favour of a cause is its advocate, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Cooperate with the French by turning over everything on Penny

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the rest follows the penny

parts.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)

indicators.note: turning over means the little word by is read backwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Working with the French by putting all one's money on a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places everything that follows after the penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To go along with others or cooperate is an idiom borrowed from the umpire's call to start a game.

clue.text: Juxtaposed with a theatrical device involving trousers for the most part

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the stage device wraps the shortened trousers

parts.note: an aside is a stage remark meant for the audience

indicators.note: for the most part drops the final letter

parts.note: longs is a word for long trousers

explanation.surface: A stage trick featuring trousers, set side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: Longs, meaning long trousers, is an old-fashioned British word.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed next to something is the sense of juxtaposed, which the phrase means.

clue.text: Persuade city fellow to stop working? Just the opposite

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so one piece sits inside the other; the clue's 'Just the opposite' swaps which goes in

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for city
Vince is a man's name, any fellow
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Trying to talk a city worker into quitting his job.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the fellow would stop the working; 'Just the opposite' swaps the roles, so the working word goes inside city plus fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone round to a view is to win them over, a synonym.

clue.text: Rex checking Peter out in Japan

indicators.note: checking means stopping or holding back, so the king letter sits inside and blocks the word

parts.note: to fizzle and disappear is to vanish
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A man called Rex checking out a man called Peter while visiting Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' looks like the country but is a verb or noun for hard black lacquer.
explanation.definitionFit: To japan is to coat with a hard glossy lacquer, the same as applying a glossy finish.

clue.text: Frequently getting to start with us for a bit of practice

indicators.note: for means taking the place of, so the new letters replace one

parts.note: to open is to start

indicators.note: a bit of picks the opening letter of the word practice

parts.note: us is the Financial Times speaking of itself, abbreviated FT

explanation.surface: Turning up often for a little practice session with us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the newspaper, the FT. It replaces the P of OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something many times is doing it frequently, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Implied without being stated by American historian

parts.note: tacit means understood without being spoken

explanation.surface: An American historian implying something left unspoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman historian, author of the Annals.

clue.text: Pants of inferior quality

definitions.meaning: in British slang, pants means rubbish or awful

explanation.surface: Trousers made badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean bad: British slang 'pants' means rubbish, and low-grade goods are shoddy.

clue.text: Talked about managing change without Henry or Victoria for instance

indicators.note: about means around, so the spoken word encloses the rest

parts.note: spoke means talked

indicators.note: managing means handling and reshaping, so the letters are rearranged
without means the Henry letter is dropped

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Discussion of how to manage change without Henry or Victoria, as if about monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarchs Henry and Victoria mislead: one is a unit symbol, the other half of the cake's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victoria sponge is a classic British cake, named after Queen Victoria; it is one example.

clue.text: Mark ignoring Iseult's last letter

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace or a spot

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of Iseult

explanation.surface: King Mark of Cornwall ignoring the last letter from Iseult, his unfaithful queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark and Iseult come from the Tristan legend; Mark is her husband. STIGMA loses the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is a Greek letter, the equivalent of S.

clue.text: Strange piece of computer software by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals a word that is pronounced the same as another

parts.note: a cookie is a small data file a website stores in your browser

explanation.surface: Some odd-seeming computer program.
explanation.definitionFit: Kooky is informal for eccentric or odd.

clue.text: Pester daughter to get out of nearby Georgia

indicators.note: to get out of means the daughter letter leaves the word

parts.note: beside means nearby
GE is the international code for the country Georgia

explanation.surface: Nagging a daughter to move away from nearby Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia is the country here, not the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset or crowd someone with demands is to pester them, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Lie when in charge after fellow gets into trouble

indicators.note: after means the in-charge letters come behind the fellow
trouble means stir up or disturb, so the letters of into are rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling a lie when a man in charge gets into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges INTO into TION. 'gets into trouble' looks like a phrase, but 'into' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A made-up story, something untrue, is a lie.

clue.text: City father not initially surprised by hint of nepotism

indicators.note: surprised means taken aback, jolted, so the letters are thrown into a new order
not initially removes the opening letter of father
a hint of gives just the opening letter of nepotism

explanation.surface: A father taken aback by a whiff of favouritism.
explanation.walkthrough: ATHER is rearranged by 'surprised' into TEHRA, then N ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: Manages to pass without honours eventually

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the pass phrase encloses the letter

parts.note: to get by is to pass, get past

indicators.note: eventually points to the final letter of honours

explanation.surface: Scraping a degree pass with no honours in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope or survive on little is an idiomatic way of saying one manages.
